normalization_levels.description: Current executable diagnostics tests compare the raised exception category through internal K sentinels or caught CPython exception classes; exact message text and traceback formatting are outside this level.
Future CPython-profile comparisons should normalize and compare exception message text, including version-specific TypeError, ValueError, SyntaxError, and UnicodeError payloads.
Future syntax-diagnostic comparisons should preserve filename, line, column, end-line, and end-column information where CPython exposes it.
Future traceback comparisons should preserve frame order, function/module names, source snippets, exception chaining display, notes, groups, and CPython traceback rendering boundaries.

adapter_diagnostic_cases.notes: Current K profile checks unbound-name category behavior, not exact NameError message text.
Current K profile checks callable arity category behavior after argument evaluation, not CPython's exact arity message strings.
Current K profile checks zero-division category behavior across supported numeric operations.
Current K profile checks invalid-subscript category behavior; CPython SyntaxWarning text and exact TypeError wording remain future work.
Current K profile checks format-spec category behavior for unsupported presentation types.
Current K profile checks decode diagnostic categories for the supported codec/error-handler subset.
Current K profile checks fromhex diagnostic categories without exact offsets or message strings.
Current K profile checks pow/modular-pow diagnostic categories for the supported numeric subset.

known_gaps: No exact CPython traceback rendering is modeled.
No exact SyntaxError filename, source line, offset, end offset, or message text is modeled.
Most runtime diagnostics are represented as exception-class sentinels, not exception instances with args.
Warning emission and filtering are not modeled except where CPython reference execution accepts warning-producing tests.
